[[File:Small dodecicosacron.stl|thumb|3D model of a small dodecicosacron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''small dodecicosacron''' (or '''small dipteral trisicosahedron''') is the dual of the [[small dodecicosahedron]] (U50). It is visually identical to the [[Small ditrigonal dodecacronic hexecontahedron]]. It has 60 intersecting [[antiparallelogram|bow-tie]]-shaped faces.

== Proportions==
Each face has two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{5}{12}+\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{5})\approx 12.661\,078\,804\,43^{\circ}</math> and two angles of <math>\arccos(-\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{20}\sqrt{5})\approx 129.657\,475\,656\,13^{\circ}</math>. The diagonals of each antiparallelogram  intersect at an angle of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{12}+\frac{19}{60}\sqrt{5})\approx 37.681\,445\,539\,45^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\frac{-44-3\sqrt{5}}{61})\approx 146.230\,659\,755\,53^{\circ}</math>. The ratio between the lengths of the long edges and the short ones equals <math>\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{5}</math>, which is the [[golden ratio]]. Part of each face lies inside the solid, hence is invisible in solid models.
